mechanism_narrative: A flat-to-improving WORKPLACES series combined with stable TRANSIT implies commuting activity is no longer deteriorating, and that stabilization will raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as weekday errands and after-work shopping recover.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays near current levels and TRANSIT does not fall further, yet RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and edges higher, more time spent at home substitutes for discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains at or above its current elevated level but RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior 4-week mean within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in TRANSIT below its current roughly 12 percent-below-baseline range signals fewer cross-city trips and less incidental shopping, which will push RETAIL_REC down within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 on the weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is persistently near -12% in the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -15 but RETAIL_REC does not fall in the following week, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains strongly positive while WORKPLACES does not recover, people are meeting necessities without broader outing patterns, and retail-and-recreation spending will stay suppressed over four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above baseline and WORKPLACES stays below baseline, yet RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean by week 4, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An upward shift in PARKS activity from its current negative level indicates outdoor recreation is substituting for indoor shopping trips, and this substitution will lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises above -10 but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the previous 2-week average within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals synchronized commuting and downtown circulation, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks more than either series alone.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES improves while TRANSIT does not, or vice versa, and RETAIL_REC still fails to exceed its last-4-week mean over the next month, the interaction claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: Because RETAIL_REC has been nearly flat while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, the most likely near-term move is mean reversion downward if home-centered routines persist; the effect should show up within one week.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline but RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days relative to the prior week, the mean-reversion mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, a renewed fall in WORKPLACES below its current level will precede weaker discretionary retail traffic, so RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -10 while TRANSIT stays below -10
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is near -4% and TRANSIT near -12% in the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES drops below -10 with TRANSIT still below -10, but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean by the end of 28 days, the hypothesis is falsified.
